transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lina Ho (Redwood CSM); Sara Lin (Procurement), Tom Becker (InfoSec), Maya Patel (Cloud), Evan Cross (Finance)

Summary:
Quick intake with procurement, finance and infosec to triage vendor on-boarding path. Main asks: DPA/MSA redline, SOC2 and ISO artifacts, technical checklist for private deployment & VPC peering, pricing band confirmation and pilot scope to run a Greybox benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Contract path: DPA redlines, MSA escalation points, pricing committee approvals
- Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, data residency
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Pilot/scoping: benchmarks, KPI (tail latency, p99, cost per 1k tokens), dataset controls
- Next steps & owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick intros — I'm Avery, AE on the Redwood side. Diego's our solutions engineer, Lina's on CS.
[00:11] Sara: Hi, Sara here with procurement. We have a few people from infosec and finance too.
[00:15] Tom: Tom Becker, head of InfoSec. Quick ask up front: we need to understand the encryption model and log retention before procurement moves forward.
[00:24] Evan: Evan Cross, finance. We'll need rough run-rate estimates for committed vs pay-as-you-go, and a decision path for who signs off on reserved capacity.
[00:33] Avery: Great, thanks. The goal today is to surface blockers — legal, security, finance — and align on pilot scope. Diego, do you want to run high level on deployment options?
[00:43] Diego: Sure. So Redwood has three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment. Hosted is fastest to start but data-in-transit encryption only and logs live in our controlled environment. Dedicated gives you isolation at the pool level and stronger SLA. Private — VPC or on-prem — is where we do customer-managed network, KMS integration, and you can keep logs in your side.
[01:05] Maya: When you say KMS integration, is that cloud-KMS only or can you do an HSM-backed approach?
[01:11] Diego: Both. We integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can also implement HSM partners for key unwrap if required by policy. There is a slight latency and ops overhead, but we can show benchmark numbers.
[01:22] Tom: Okay, audit logs — what retention windows are typical and can they be pushed to our SIEM?
[01:27] Diego: Logs can be exported to your SIEM via streaming; retention is configurable on your side for private; for hosted we retain X days by default but we can extend under enterprise contracts. I'll follow up with exact numbers and an export diagram.
[01:38] Sara: On the legal side — we usually need a DPA and MSA, standard redlines. Our pricing committee requires an expected monthly commit before we go to legal. Evan, you'll lead that piece?
[01:47] Evan: Yep. We want a 12 month committed band if possible but need options. Can you give committed pricing tiers vs on-demand today?
[01:53] Avery: We'll send a spreadsheet — high level: hosted per-token, embeddings and rerank separate lines; dedicated has a reserved monthly fee plus usage; private is a license/entitlement plus ops add-on. We'll put example math for 100M tokens/month to show delta.
[02:08] Lina: Also worth noting Optimize tooling — we can recommend batching + cache settings to reduce unit costs. We'll include those suggestions in the pilot plan.
[02:16] Maya: For private/VPC, can you support VPC peering or PrivateLink? We can't allow internet egress for inference calls.
[02:22] Diego: Yes, VPC peering and PrivateLink supported. For private we can deploy the runtime in your VPC or in a customer-dedicated subnet. We'll include a network diagram; there are egress control knobs.
[02:34] Tom: One of our policy items: key rotation and split-key custody — do you support customer-managed keys where Redwood never sees key material?
[02:40] Diego: Yes, customer-managed KMS where keys are used for envelope encryption so Redwood doesn't have plaintext keys. We'll document the flow.
[02:48] Sara: On the DPA, we have a standard data residency clause: no data replication outside EMEA for EU customers. How flexible is Redwood on region locking?
[02:56] Avery: We have region pinning for dedicated/private, and hosting region for hosted API — we can keep data in EU regions but need to map model availability. Some model variants may not be in all regions immediately. We'll note that as a constraint.
[03:09] Evan: For procurement, timeline is tight — we'd like legal to sign in three weeks if possible. What slippage do you usually see on DPA redlines?
[03:16] Avery: For standard customers it's usually 1–2 weeks; enterprise exceptions can take longer. If you send redlines we'll route to legal for triage and propose a path.
[03:23] Tom: We also need to validate their SOC2 and ISO attestation and ideally have the pen test summary.
[03:30] Lina: We'll upload SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, and a summarised pen-test redaction as soon as sign-off.
[03:36] Maya: About pilot: we want to run a greybox throughput test with synthetic queries mimicking our conversational flows, plus a sample dataset for quality checks. Can you support a GPU-backed test for 24–48 hours?
[03:46] Diego: Absolutely. For a realistic test we'll recommend dedicated inference with pinned model and sequence lengths matching your traffic. We can pre-warm KV caches to approximate production state. We should log p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:58] Evan: And cost transparency — will the pilot show expected monthly cost for a scaled profile?
[04:04] Avery: Yes, post-pilot we provide a projection sheet that maps observed throughput/latency to unit economics and gives recommendations like model quantization or batching to reduce costs.
[04:12] Tom: One more security question: does Redwood provide field-level encryption for sensitive fields so we can tokenize or redact PII before sending requests?
[04:19] Diego: We don't provide field-level pre-ingest tokenization out of the box, but we can support a proxy pattern where you perform tokenization in your VPC before hitting the runtime. We'll document patterns.
[04:30] Speaker 1: (mumble) and the legal, um, indemnity table — how flexible is MSA?
[04:36] Avery: Typical MSA redlines around indemnity are handled case-by-case; we'll have legal look at the redline. If Helix has specific carveouts we can surface them early to avoid last-minute surprises.
[04:46] Sara: Our review also needs to map to our supplier risk framework — low/medium/high. What category do you usually fall into for finance apps?
[04:53] Lina: Usually medium; we provide SOC2 and have enterprise controls for private deployments which can bump you to low in your scoring because of isolation.
[05:01] Maya: Operational questions — how are secrets stored on a private deployment? Is there a vault integration?
[05:07] Diego: We integrate with Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and we can chain to your HSM for key wrapping. We'll include options in the runbook.
[05:16] Tom: Audit cadence: do you support third-party audits on private deployments?
[05:20] Avery: We support audit rights under enterprise agreements and can provide logs and artifacts for on-site or remote audits. We'll capture the scope in the DPA/MSA.
[05:29] Evan: About pricing approvals — our procurement committee needs a two-tier approval: Finance (me) and then ExecOps for anything above threshold. How does Redwood structure consumption reporting?
[05:39] Lina: We provide per-token usage reports, route/model breakdowns, and cost allocation tags you can map into your billing system. We'll demo the console during the pilot.
[05:49] Sara: On the DPA redline, we have a particular requirement around subprocessing and subcontractor lists. We'll need Redwood's subprocessors and where backups/snapshots live.
[05:58] Diego: We'll list subprocessors and the data flow for snapshots — for private deployment snapshots are customer controlled; for hosted we manage backups but can restrict retention.
[06:08] Tom: If we were to run private (VPC), what's the ops model for patching and upgrades? We can't accept breaking changes automatically.
[06:15] Diego: For private/on-prem deployments we provide a control plane and can schedule maintenance windows; there's a canary rollout path and pinned model versions so you control when to accept a model upgrade. That said, security patches have a defined SLA.
[06:28] Maya: That's good. We'll need the maintenance window policy documented because our platform has nightly backups we don't want to overlap.
[06:35] Avery: We'll include a maintenance windows doc and recommended scheduling.
[06:39] Evan: Can you provide an example SLA with latency targets per p99 and credits? Our SLA team expects clear SLOs.
[06:46] Diego: Yes, for dedicated we provide p95/p99 latency targets and availability SLA. For hosted the numbers are published but can be tightened under contract. We'll attach a sample SLA.
[06:56] Sara: For procurement gating: first step is DPA review and SOC2 verification; second is a pilot which will then feed into pricing committee; third is legal signature. Does that sound right?
[07:05] Avery: Yes that's our typical path. If InfoSec green-lights the security artifacts we can start a constrained pilot while legal is triaging redlines to compress timeline.
[07:13] Tom: From our side, redline triage depends on seeing specific KMS flow diagrams and proof of no-plaintext-handling.
[07:19] Diego: We'll diagram envelope encryption flows and share a sequence diagram with exact touchpoints.
[07:26] Speaker 2 (mumbled): also, data residency for backups, can you confirm locality?
[07:31] Diego: We'll call that out; hosted backups are region-local but some metadata may be global; we'll clarify.
[07:38] Maya: One operational ask — can we get a short runbook for onboarding dev teams so they can spin up a staging route with test tokens?
[07:44] Lina: Yes, we have a developer quickstart for self-serve onboarding that we'll tailor with your network steps and token provisioning.
[07:52] Sara: A note on the pricing committee — they will ask for a committed discount threshold. Do you have a baseline discount schedule?
[07:59] Avery: We'll provide a baseline tiered discount schedule by commit band; it's flexible depending on length of term and support add-ons. We'll send the spreadsheet.
[08:06] Evan: If we do a 12 month commit, do you offer hardware isolation or guaranteed pool sizing?
[08:13] Diego: That's the dedicated model — reserved GPU pools and we can contract throughput guarantees. We'll include typical commit/throughput mapping.
[08:21] Tom: About data deletion — if a contract ends, can you purge data and provide attestation?
[08:26] Avery: Yes, we provide data deletion and certification per contract. For private deployments, you can perform deletion locally. For hosted we will issue a deletion attest once completed.
[08:36] Maya: For pilot logistics, Diego, what do you need from our side to stand up the test?
[08:40] Diego: We'll need a small set of sample queries, representative seq lengths, expected concurrency and traffic profile, VPC peering info if private, and an agree on data handling for the quality set. Also service account for access.
[08:50] Maya: We'll prepare that. What about model variants? We use a mixture of LLMs for retrieval + generation — can you support tool-calling or function-style structured outputs?
[08:59] Diego: We support structured outputs and function-calling semantics. For retrieval-augmented flows, we recommend embeddings + reranker config; we'll include recommended model picks.
[09:08] Tom: On legal exceptions — we sometimes require limited indemnity for regulated lines of business. Are you open to carveouts?
[09:15] Avery: Legal will review carveouts; from a product side we can provide controls that reduce risk exposure. We'll escalate to legal once we receive the specific requests.
[09:23] Sara: Ok, timeline recap: DPA redline to Redwood by end of day 2026-03-23, Redwood to respond with revised DPA + security pack by 2026-03-25; pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-30.
[09:36] Avery: That works. We'll also include cost projection scenarios.
[09:40] Evan: Great. Any blockers from infosec?
[09:43] Tom: Just the KMS/HSM confirmation and audit artefacts. Once those are in we'll green-light pilot.
[09:50] Avery: We'll prioritize those and follow up.
[09:54] Lina: I'll share a tailored quickstart and the Optimize suggestions for batching.
[09:59] Sara: Thanks everyone.
[10:01] Avery: Thanks, we'll send the artifacts in the next two business days.

End transcript.

References & links mentioned during call:
